newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Front page editorial urges agricultural departments to summarise experience in reaping good harvests for past two years, so as to achieve another good harvest this year.

- Commentary proposes state enterprises improve their efficiency by cutting the number of employees. It cites example of Yanzhou Mining (Group) Company that succeeded in increasing efficiency fourfold by cutting back on number of miners and adopting advanced technology and equipment.
- Politburo member Hu Jintao urges study of politics
CHINA SECURITIES
- Hong Hu, vice minister of State Commission for Economic Restructuring, says China's experiment to turn 2,000 selected state firms into new share-holding companies to be completed by end-1997
- Chen Qingtai, vice minister of State Economic and Trade Commission says prudent approach should be taken in transforming state debts into shares
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Industrial and Commercial Bank of China agrees to make 1.0 billion yuan in loans to Sichuan provincial power company
ECONOMIC DAILY
- State Adminstration of Taxation issues circular ordering cuts or abolition of taxes for poverty-ridden farmers
- Official survey finds consumer satisfaction index rises in first quarter due to falling inflation and stable income, but confidence index falls due to high property prices
MARKET DAILY
- China steel industry faces unfavourable factors likely to cut profits by 8.0 billion yuan in 1997
- China's yuan seen strong against dollar throughout 1997
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- China says not to excavate any ancient emperors' tombs because of lack of advanced technology
CHINA DAILY
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong arrives for visit
- Communist Party cadres urged to be clean, honest
- Xi'an shuts 50 advertising firms for illegal practices
- Minister of Public Security Tao Siju calls for all-out war on crime
